subject: Discovery Recap & Proposed PoC Plan — FastRetail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap & Proposed PoC Plan — FastRetail

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and a proposed PoC/integration plan so we can align next steps. Please flag anything I missed or that you'd like changed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High inference costs on peak traffic and unpredictable token billing from current provider
- Latency spikes during promotional bursts (affects checkout and search UX)
- Lack of transparent per-route observability and cost attribution
- Data residency and VPC isolation requirements for certain EU customers

Current stack / environment:
- Backend: TypeScript (Node.js) microservices on ECS Fargate
- Caching: Redis for short-term prefix cache
- Metrics: Datadog; logs to central S3 bucket
- Current LLM vendor: managed API with limited batching controls

Success criteria for PoC (your priorities):
1) End-to-end latency for the product-search autocomplete flow <= 200ms p50, <= 350ms p95
2) Cost per 1M tokens reduced by >= 30% vs current baseline
3) Transparent per-route cost & latency dashboards for product and checkout routes
4) Integration with TypeScript/Node stack and sample deployable reference

Proposed PoC & onboarding plan (suggested timeline):
- Week 0 (this week): Align owners, get NDA/POC agreement in place if needed; exchange security checklist
- Week 1: Provision PoC API keys (hosted/dedicated options), share SDK samples for Node and Python; initial smoke test against a staging dataset
- Week 2: Integrate SDK in a single microservice (autocomplete route) + enable prefix caching; run load ramp to observe latency
- Week 3: Measure p50/p95 and cost metrics; iterate on batching and KV caching config; attach Datadog tracing hooks
- Week 4: PoC report + recommendations for production rollout and estimated committed capacity/costs

Owners / contacts:
- Marissa Cole (AE) — PoC coordinator, schedules demos and success review
- Ben Carter (Solutions Engineer) — technical lead for integration, will own SDK samples and on-call during integration
- Samantha Lee (FastRetail) — primary engineering contact for integration and test data

Integration notes / compatibility:
- Redwood provides REST + streaming WebSocket APIs; SDKs available for Node (TypeScript) and Python.
- We support running in a VPC / private deployment for tighter data controls (can discuss Dedicated vs Private options).
- We will provide a small sample repo (Node) and a Dockerized example to drop into your CI.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.xlsx (PoC milestones and acceptance criteria)

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm the PoC owners and the staging environment details (DNS, API gateway)
2) Can you share a 1-hour slot next week for a kickoff? I suggest Wed 3/10 10:00–11:00 PT — happy to adjust.
3) Any additional compliance constraints we should pre-clear (e.g., contract language for data retention)?

If that looks good I'll loop Ben on the kickoff invite and share the sample repo ahead of the meeting.

Thanks — talk soon,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Proposed PoC Plan — FastRetail

Hi Marissa — thanks for the tidy recap, this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / notes from our side:

- Tech stack: our production services are TypeScript (Node 18) — we actually prefer TypeScript client examples over plain JS.
- Primary objectives are throughput/cost; latency targets are correct. For p95 we may accept up to 400ms during heavy promos if cost savings are substantial.
- We will need a Dockerized example and a simple CI step (GitHub Actions) to run the smoke tests in our staging pipeline.
- Security: SOC2 is important but we also need to confirm KMS integrations for key wrapping and an audit log export cadence.

Ben — pinging you for any questions on the integration side.

I can do Wed 10 Mar 10:00–11:00 PT for kickoff. Please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Samantha
Head of ML Ops | FastRetail
samantha.lee@fastretail.com

Thanks Marissa / Samantha — quick note from the engineering side.

Plan for PoC integration (technical):
- Day 1: Provide Node (TypeScript) SDK package and a Python example for comparison. SDK will include streaming and non-streaming call patterns.
- Day 2–3: Share Dockerized sample + GitHub Actions workflow that runs a smoke test against staging.
- Batching & caching: we'll enable configurable continuous batching and prefix KV cache; I'll include recommended defaults for your autocomplete workload.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration is supported for private deployments; for hosted we can provide per-customer key wrapping and audit logs exports.

I'll attach a short integration-checklist.md with the exact API endpoints, required IAM rules, and a sequence of smoke tests. Ben (internal) will join the kickoff to walk through the sample repo.

Can you confirm the staging URL and whether the staging environment can accept a short-lived API key we issue?
